document_metadata.title: 1、INT. COMIC BOOK STORE - DAY
document_metadata.summary: Steve-Dave receives a check and mocking note from Holden and Banky, compensating for the broken window; Walt wants revenge, but legal action is dismissed.

entities.name: Holden and Banky arrive at the comic book store to purchase their named comic
entities.description: Holden and Banky enter the store, approach the counter, and present the comic book 'Bluntman and Chronic' for purchase, engaging in banter with the store staff.

entities.name: Banky expresses pride over seeing his name on the comic book cover
entities.description: Banky points out his name on the cover of the comic book, expressing excitement and pride over the recognition and commercial success of their work.

entities.name: Holden shows disinterest in the comic book release
entities.description: Holden flips through the comic with visible disapproval, downplaying the significance of the release and expressing that the work is beneath their artistic potential.

entities.name: Steve-Dave and Walt mock Holden and Banky at the counter
entities.description: Steve-Dave, the store manager, and Walt, a fan, exchange sarcastic remarks about Holden and Banky being 'local celebrities' and joke about profiting from their autographs.

entities.name: Walt defends the card game 'Crimson Mystical Mages' from mockery
entities.description: Walt responds to Banky's insult about their card game by clarifying it is 'Crimson Mystical Mages', emphasizing its complexity and contrasting it with crude humor.

entities.name: Crimson Mystical Mages Card Game Session At The Comic Book Store
entities.description: Steve-Dave and Walt are engaged in an ongoing session of the strategic card game 'Crimson Mystical Mages' at the store counter, which is interrupted by Holden and Banky's arrival.
entities.summary: Steve-Dave and Walt are engaged in an ongoing session of the strategic card game 'Crimson Mystical Mages' at the store counter, which is interrupted by Holden and Banky's arrival.

entities.name: Comic-Toast
entities.description: A named retail establishment where comic books and card games are sold, serving as the primary setting for the scene.
entities.summary:
A named retail establishment where comic books and card games are sold, serving as the primary setting for the scene.
A specific retail store specializing in comics, where Alyssa purchases a comic and an incident occurs with Steve-Dave.

entities.name: Holden Mcneil
entities.description: A comic book artist who co-created 'Bluntman and Chronic' and is unenthusiastic about the release of the second issue despite having his name on it.
entities.summary: A former comic book collaborator of Banky Edwards, co-creator of 'Bluntman and Chronic', makes a quiet appearance at a comic book signing, sharing a nonverbal moment with Banky amid past tensions over their work and personal relationships.

entities.name: Banky Edwards
entities.description: A comic book artist and co-creator of 'Bluntman and Chronic' who takes pride in seeing his name on the comic book cover and defends its commercial success.
entities.summary: A comic book artist and co-creator of 'Bluntman and Chronic,' known for inking and coloring, also created 'Baby Dave' and is signing copies at a comic event, reflecting on his collaboration and fallout with Holden McNeil.

entities.name: Steve-Dave
entities.description: The manager of the comic book store who mocks Holden and Banky while playing a card game with Walt.
entities.summary: The comic book store manager mocks Holden and Banky during a card game with Walt, asserts dominance, and reacts angrily when a garbage can crashes through the window during Holden and Alyssa's visit.

entities.name: Walt
entities.description: A fan-boy customer at the comic book store who plays 'Crimson Mystical Mages' with Steve-Dave and defends the game from mockery.
entities.summary: A fan-boy regular at the comic book store plays 'Crimson Mystical Mages' with Steve-Dave, defends the game from mockery, expresses frustration over life-power point disparity, and reacts to a sudden intrusion by diving for cover.

entities.name: Bluntman And Chronic Comic Book
entities.description: A comic book featuring the characters Bluntman and Chronic, co-created by Holden and Banky, with their names printed on the cover.
entities.summary:
A comic book featuring the characters Bluntman and Chronic, co-created by Holden and Banky, with their names printed on the cover.
A comic book featuring the characters Bluntman and Chronic, co-created by Holden and Banky, which has become commercially available.

entities.name: Crimson Mystical Mages
entities.description: A complex card game played by Steve-Dave and Walt at the comic book store, presented as more sophisticated than typical humor-based games.

entities.name: Steve-Dave and Walt harshly criticize Holden and Banky's comic work
entities.description: Steve-Dave and Walt confront Holden and Banky, denouncing their comic 'Bluntman and Chronic' as talentless, mediocre, and damaging to the reputation of comics, while asserting their own disdain for the creators.

entities.name: Steve-Dave mocks the 'Stinky-palm' move from Bluntman and Chronic
entities.description: Steve-Dave ridicules a specific element from the comic 'Bluntman and Chronic'—the 'Stinky-palm' move—using it as evidence of the comic's poor quality.

entities.name: Steve-Dave declares Comic-Toast a no-flattery zone for untalented creators
entities.description: Steve-Dave emphasizes that at Comic-Toast, unlike other places, Holden and Banky will not receive praise because he and Walt genuinely believe their work has no merit.

entities.name: Steve-Dave flips off Holden and Banky before resuming the card game
entities.description: After verbally berating Holden and Banky, Steve-Dave extends his middle fingers toward them in a gesture of contempt, then returns to playing 'Crimson Mystical Mages' with Walt.

entities.name: Holden and Banky react to the criticism with shock and leave
entities.description: Following the harsh critique from Steve-Dave and Walt, Holden and Banky remain silent, exchange a nudge, and exit the comic book store without further confrontation.

entities.name: Steve-Dave and the Fan-boy celebrate and continue playing Crimson Mystical Mages
entities.description: After the confrontation, Steve-Dave and another player (the Fan-boy) slap hands in camaraderie and return to their ongoing game session of 'Crimson Mystical Mages'.

entities.name: Walt wins a card in the Crimson Mystical Mages game
entities.description: Walt announces he has a powerful dragon card and successfully captures Steve-Dave's elf card during their game of 'Crimson Mystical Mages'.

entities.name: Comic-Toast
entities.description: A named comic book store where the confrontation and card game take place.
entities.summary:
A named comic book store where the confrontation and card game take place.

entities.name: Fan-boy
entities.description: A character who celebrates with Steve-Dave after Holden and Banky leave and continues playing Crimson Mystical Mages, showing enthusiasm for the game and alignment with Steve-Dave's opinions.

entities.name: dragon card
entities.description: A card in the Crimson Mystical Mages game that has forty power-ups and twelve life points, used by Walt to win against his opponent.

entities.name: elf card
entities.description: A card in the Crimson Mystical Mages game that is lost by Walt's opponent when defeated by the dragon card.

entities.name: Words Up - Minority Voices In Comics Panel Discussion
entities.description: A panel discussion at a comic convention featuring creators discussing representation and minority voices in the comics industry, with five participants seated at a table and an audience present.
entities.summary: A panel of five comic creators discusses representation and minority voices in the comics industry at a convention, with audience attendance.

entities.name: Hooper presents his comic book 'White-Hating Coon' at the panel
entities.description: Hooper holds up his comic book titled 'White-Hating Coon' during the panel discussion, introducing it as a work that rejects stereotypical naming and asserts Black empowerment.

entities.name: Hooper criticizes racist naming of African-American characters in comics
entities.description: Hooper delivers a critique of historically racist character names given to African-American superheroes and villains by white creators, listing examples such as Black Panther and Black Lightning.

entities.name: Audience member points out the woman at the panel is white
entities.description: A voice from the crowd interrupts Hooper's speech to note that one of the panelists, a striking girl, is white, prompting a brief pause in the discussion.

entities.name: Hooper declares the end of Black minstrelsy in comics
entities.description: Hooper proclaims that Black characters in comics and sci-fi/fantasy will no longer be portrayed in subservient or stereotypical roles, asserting a new era of authenticity and respect for Black identity.

entities.name: panel discussion
entities.description: A generic setting where the event takes place, referring to the immediate scene with creators at a table and an audience.

entities.name: Hooper
entities.description: A comic book creator and speaker at the panel discussion who presents his work and critiques racist naming practices in comics while promoting his own comic book.
entities.summary: A comic book creator critiques racist naming in comics and promotes his work, while a performer uses a 'Black Rage' persona; a participant offers a queer reading of Archie and Jughead, challenging Banky; Holden's friend invites him to a club event, and mutual connections link Holden and Alyssa.

entities.name: striking Girl
entities.description: A female comic creator sitting at the panel discussion, noted for her appearance and presence among the speakers.

entities.name: racist naming in comics
entities.description: The practice of assigning racially charged or stereotypical names to African-American characters in comic books, criticized during the panel discussion.

entities.name: comic book 'White-Hating Coon'
entities.description: A comic book created by Hooper, presented during the panel as an example of anti-racist storytelling and featuring the character Maleekwa.

entities.name: placards with names
entities.description: Name tags placed in front of the creators sitting at the panel discussion, indicating their identities to the audience.

entities.name: banner reading 'WORDS UP - MINORITY VOICES IN COMICS'
entities.description: A backdrop banner displayed behind the panelists, identifying the title and theme of the event.

entities.name: Black minstrelsy in comics
entities.description: A derogatory representation of Black characters in comics historically shaped by white creators, which Hooper declares to be ending.

entities.name: Holden and Banky enter the panel discussion and sit in the front
entities.description: Holden and Banky arrive at the Words Up - Minority Voices In Comics panel discussion and take seats at the front of the audience.

entities.name: Holden calls out during Hooper's speech to defend Lando Calrissian
entities.description: Holden interrupts Hooper's speech by shouting that Lando Calrissian is a positive Black role model in science fiction and fantasy.

entities.name: Hooper reacts angrily to Holden's interruption and denounces Lando Calrissian
entities.description: Hooper demands to know who spoke, then dismisses Lando Calrissian as an 'Uncle Tom nigger' and criticizes the Star Wars narrative for reinforcing white dominance.

entities.name: Hooper reinterprets Star Wars as a story of racial oppression and gentrification
entities.description: Hooper argues that Star Wars symbolizes racial dynamics, portraying Luke Skywalker as a white supremacist figure and Darth Vader as a powerful Black spiritual figure whose domain is taken over by whites.

entities.name: Banky questions the meaning of 'Nubian' and later comments on the Star Wars plot
entities.description: Banky asks what a 'Nubian' is during Hooper's speech, and later jokingly refers to the conflict in Star Wars as an 'Intergalactic Civil War'.

entities.name: Holden argues that Vader and Luke's reconciliation undermines Hooper's interpretation
entities.description: Holden points out that Vader is revealed to be Luke's father and that they reconcile in Return of the Jedi, challenging Hooper's racial reading of the saga.

entities.name: Hooper condemns Return of the Jedi for implying Black people want to be white
entities.description: Hooper responds to Holden by claiming that Vader's unmasking as a white man in Jedi is deeply offensive, suggesting the film promotes internalized racism by implying 'deep inside, we all want to be white'.

entities.name: Banky expresses agreement with the idea that people want to be white
entities.description: Banky casually states that the idea of wanting to be white might be true, further provoking Hooper and highlighting ideological tension in the discussion.

entities.name: during the speech
entities.description: A relative temporal anchor indicating the time frame within the scene when Holden and Banky enter and the subsequent exchange occurs.

entities.name: Holden Mcneil
entities.description: A participant in the panel discussion who challenges Hooper's interpretation of Star Wars by defending Lando Calrissian as a positive black role model.
entities.summary: Multiple individuals engage in various discussions at a comic event, including debates on Star Wars, observations on performances, reflections on personal history, and reactions to changing environments and personal stories.

entities.name: Banky Edwards
entities.description: A companion of Holden who attends the panel discussion and makes comments questioning the meaning of 'Nubian' and later agreeing with the idea that people want to be white.
entities.summary: A comic book artist collaborates with Holden, defends his artistic process, participates in a panel, and reacts skeptically to social plans, while engaging in discussions on identity, representation, and comic interpretations.

entities.name: Science Fiction/Fantasy
entities.description: A genre category referenced in the discussion as a realm where racial representation and symbolism are being analyzed.

entities.name: lightsaber
entities.description: A weapon in the Star Wars universe that symbolizes power and is referenced in Hooper's interpretation of racial dynamics in the films.

entities.name: Hooper draws a nine millimeter and fires at Banky
entities.description: Hooper pulls a gun from his belt, aims at Banky, and shoots, causing Banky to fall forward into the crowd.

entities.name: Crowd reacts to gunfire and scatters
entities.description: After Hooper fires the gun, the crowd screams in panic and begins to flee the scene.

entities.name: Hooper jumps over the table and declares Black Rage
entities.description: Hooper leaps over a table, raises his fists, and shouts 'Black Rage!' repeatedly in a performative outburst.

entities.name: Holden laughs while sitting in his chair
entities.description: While chaos unfolds around him, Holden remains seated and laughs at the unfolding performance.

entities.name: Hooper breaks character and reveals the gun is loaded with blanks
entities.description: Hooper lifts Banky's head, speaks in a different tone, and explains that the gun contained blank rounds and that the performance is pre-approved.

entities.name: Banky expresses surprise at the 'Black Rage' performance
entities.description: Banky comments that he wasn't warned about the 'Black Rage' outburst and admits he nearly lost control from fear.

entities.name: Holden questions the legality and plausibility of the performance
entities.description: Holden expresses disbelief that Hooper can stage such acts without police intervention, prompting Banky to explain they are on the wrong coast for that to happen.

entities.name: Hooper explains the publisher's support for the theatrical image
entities.description: Hooper reveals that his publisher not only condones but insists on the 'Black Rage' persona to sell books, despite his true identity.

entities.name: Hooper kisses Banky on the lips
entities.description: In a moment of intimacy or provocation, Hooper kisses Banky fully on the mouth, which Banky reacts to by wiping his lips.

entities.name: Banky rejects romantic involvement with Hooper
entities.description: After being kissed, Banky clarifies that while he will play Hooper's victim in performances, he will not engage in a romantic or physical relationship.

entities.name: stage
entities.description: A physical setting where Hooper performs the 'Black Rage' act and interacts with Banky before stepping off.

entities.name: crowd
entities.description: A physical gathering of people present at the performance, where Banky falls and the audience scatters.

entities.name: floor
entities.description: The surface where Banky's head lands after being shot with blanks and where Hooper picks it up.

entities.name: chair
entities.description: The seat where Holden remains during the performance, laughing at the events unfolding.

entities.name: Hooper
entities.description: A performer who stages a dramatic act involving a fake gun and the 'Black Rage' persona to maintain a public image aligned with his book's theme.
entities.summary: A comic book creator critiques racist naming in comics and promotes his work, while a performer uses a 'Black Rage' persona; a participant offers a queer reading of Archie and Jughead, challenging Banky; Holden's friend invites him to a club event, and mutual connections link Holden and Alyssa.

entities.name: Banky Edwards
entities.description: A participant in Hooper's performance, playing the role of victim, and reacting with surprise and discomfort to both the act and an unexpected kiss.
entities.summary: A comic book artist collaborates with Holden, defends his artistic process, participates in a panel, and reacts skeptically to social plans, while engaging in discussions on identity, representation, and comic interpretations.

entities.name: Holden Mcneil
entities.description: An observer of the performance who questions its legality and authenticity while remaining seated and amused.
entities.summary: Multiple individuals engage in various discussions at a comic event, including debates on Star Wars, observations on performances, reflections on personal history, and reactions to changing environments and personal stories.

entities.name: nine millimeter
entities.description: A handgun used by Hooper during his performance, later revealed to be loaded with blanks.

entities.name: Opiate
entities.description: The publishing company that supports and legally clears Hooper's theatrical performances as part of his public image.
entities.summary:
The publishing company that supports and legally clears Hooper's theatrical performances as part of his public image.
Hooper's publisher, an organization that legally clears and actively encourages his controversial public performances to promote book sales.

entities.name: Black Rage
entities.description: A theatrical persona and performance motif adopted by Hooper to align with the perceived expectations of his audience and market.
entities.summary: A theatrical persona and performance motif adopted by Hooper to align with the perceived expectations of his audience and market.

entities.name: Alyssa confronts Hooper about dominating the panel
entities.description: Alyssa approaches Hooper angrily, shoving and slapping him, expressing frustration that he consistently overshadows her on panels despite her being invited to speak.

entities.name: Hooper introduces Alyssa to Holden and Banky
entities.description: Hooper presents Alyssa Jones to Holden and Banky, identifying her as the author of 'Idiosyncratic Routine' and commenting on their shared panel history.

entities.name: Banky insults Alyssa's book as 'chick stuff'
entities.description: After claiming to have read her work, Banky dismissively refers to Alyssa's book as 'cute' but categorizes it as 'chick stuff,' prompting a rebuke from Holden.

entities.name: Holden reprimands Banky for his comment
entities.description: Holden physically hits Banky and gives him a disapproving look in response to his sexist remark about Alyssa's book.

entities.name: Alyssa mocks Banky for being an inker
entities.description: After Holden explains Banky's role, Alyssa sarcastically responds with 'Oh. You trace!', belittling his creative contribution.

entities.name: Holden compliments Alyssa and expresses interest in meeting again
entities.description: Holden shakes Alyssa's hand, tells her he enjoys her book, and expresses surprise they haven't met at previous conventions.

entities.name: Alyssa delivers a sarcastic remark about racial and gender dynamics on panels
entities.description: Alyssa tells Holden that if he wants to be on panels with her regularly, he should either 'lose the dick or change your skin tone,' criticizing the tokenization of marginalized voices.

entities.name: Hooper invites the group for a post-rave drink
entities.description: Hooper suggests that the group stay in the city for a drink after the event, framing it as a social outing following the panel.

entities.name: Holden agrees to stay for drinks despite Banky's hesitation
entities.description: When Banky indicates they should leave, Holden overrides him and accepts Hooper's invitation, signaling his willingness to continue socializing.

entities.name: Hooper claims Archie and Jughead were lovers
entities.description: Hooper states that Archie and Jughead had a romantic relationship, with Archie as the submissive partner and Jughead as the dominant one, citing Jughead's hat as symbolic of his role.

entities.name: Banky rejects Hooper's interpretation of Archie comics
entities.description: Banky angrily dismisses Hooper's claim about Archie and Jughead's relationship, expressing outrage and discomfort with the suggestion.

entities.name: Holden acknowledges ambiguity in Archie's romantic choices
entities.description: Holden comments that Hooper has a valid point, noting that Archie never definitively chose between Betty and Veronica, suggesting possible bisexuality or indecision.

entities.name: Banky accuses Archie of wanting a threesome with Betty and Veronica
entities.description: Banky argues that Archie's inability to choose between Betty and Veronica stems from his desire to have both in a sexual relationship, not from any homosexual tendencies.

entities.name: Hooper challenges Banky to buy a clue with a dollar
entities.description: Hooper hands Banky a dollar and sarcastically instructs him to go to the corner store to 'buy himself a clue' about the true nature of Archie's character.

entities.name: Banky insults Hooper and refuses the dollar
entities.description: Banky tells Hooper to 'eat it' and calls him 'Urkel' in a derogatory manner, rejecting the offered dollar and escalating the tension.

entities.name: Hooper warns Banky about using the name Urkel
entities.description: Hooper confronts Banky for calling him Urkel, indicating that the nickname is offensive or provocative in their context.

entities.name: Banky confronts Hooper and demands he return to the comic store
entities.description: Banky stands up and insists that Hooper accompany him back across the street to purchase a large number of Archie comics to prove that Archie was heterosexual.

entities.name: Hooper agrees to go with Banky as a mock therapist
entities.description: Hooper playfully frames himself as a 'mother-therapist' who will help Banky work through his emotional conflict about Archie's sexuality, then slides out of the booth to leave.

entities.name: Hooper delivers speech criticizing racist naming of African-American comic characters
entities.description: Hooper addresses the audience at a panel discussion, denouncing the historically racist naming conventions used for African-American characters in comics created by white artists and writers.

entities.name: Audience member points out female character is white
entities.description: During Hooper's speech, a voice from the crowd interrupts to note that the female character being discussed is white, prompting Hooper to briefly react with surprise.

entities.name: Hooper introduces his comic book character Maleekwa
entities.description: Hooper presents his comic book character Maleekwa as a strong, culturally proud black hero and contrasts him with stereotypical portrayals in mainstream comics.

entities.name: Hooper declares shift in representation of black characters in comics
entities.description: Hooper proclaims that black characters in comics will no longer be portrayed as minstrels and demands respect for black voices in science fiction and fantasy storytelling.

entities.name: Holden challenges Hooper's argument with reference to Lando Calrissian
entities.description: Holden interrupts Hooper's speech by shouting 'Bullshit!' and asserts that Lando Calrissian is a positive black role model in science fiction who piloted the Millennium Falcon.

entities.name: Hooper confronts Holden about his interruption
entities.description: After hearing Holden's challenge, Hooper turns sharply and demands to know who spoke out against him during the panel discussion.

entities.name: Holden stands and defends Lando Calrissian as a black role model
entities.description: Holden stands up in the audience and reiterates his point that Lando Calrissian represents a positive black presence in science fiction and fantasy media.

entities.name: Words Up - Minority Voices In Comics Panel Discussion
entities.description: A formally organized panel discussion featuring five comic creators, focused on amplifying underrepresented perspectives in the comics industry, with an audience in attendance.
entities.summary: A panel of five comic creators discusses representation and minority voices in the comics industry at a convention, with audience attendance.

entities.name: panel discussion
entities.description: A physical setting where the event takes place, specifically a room hosting a panel discussion with creators seated at a table.

entities.name: Hooper
entities.description: A comic book creator and speaker at the panel discussion who criticizes the naming of African-American comic characters and introduces his own character, Maleekwa.
entities.summary: A comic book creator critiques racist naming in comics and promotes his work, while a performer uses a 'Black Rage' persona; a participant offers a queer reading of Archie and Jughead, challenging Banky; Holden's friend invites him to a club event, and mutual connections link Holden and Alyssa.

entities.name: Holden Mcneil
entities.description: A participant in the audience who challenges Hooper's argument by citing Lando Calrissian as a positive black role model in science fiction.
entities.summary: Multiple individuals engage in various discussions at a comic event, including debates on Star Wars, observations on performances, reflections on personal history, and reactions to changing environments and personal stories.

entities.name: Banky Edwards
entities.description: An individual who enters the panel discussion with Holden and sits in the audience.
entities.summary: A comic book artist collaborates with Holden, defends his artistic process, participates in a panel, and reacts skeptically to social plans, while engaging in discussions on identity, representation, and comic interpretations.

entities.name: audience member
entities.description: An unidentified individual in the crowd who points out that the female character being discussed is white.

entities.name: striking Girl
entities.description: A female comic book creator sitting at the panel table, noted for her appearance.

entities.name: white artists and writers in the comic industry
entities.description: A systemic force criticized by Hooper for perpetuating racist representations and controlling narratives in comic books.

entities.name: placards with names
entities.description: Name tags placed in front of the creators at the panel table indicating their identities.

entities.name: banner reading WORDS UP - MINORITY VOICES IN COMICS
entities.description: A displayed banner behind the panelists that identifies the name and theme of the event.

entities.name: comic book titled White-Hating Coon
entities.description: A comic book held up by Hooper during his speech, presented as an example of his work that avoids what he sees as racist naming conventions.

entities.name: black tribe that established the first society on the planet
entities.description: A mythologized ancestral group claimed by Hooper to be the origin of his character Maleekwa and symbolic of black superiority in human origins.

entities.name: Hooper denounces Lando Calrissian as an Uncle Tom figure
entities.description: Hooper angrily rejects Lando Calrissian as a symbol of racial betrayal, calling him an 'Uncle Tom nigger' and expressing disdain for white audiences invoking the character as a positive representation.

entities.name: Hooper reinterprets Star Wars as allegory for racial oppression
entities.description: Hooper presents a critical narrative of the Star Wars films, framing Luke Skywalker as a white supremacist figure and Darth Vader as a powerful black spiritual leader whose identity is ultimately compromised by whiteness.

entities.name: Banky questions meaning of 'Nubian'
entities.description: During Hooper's rant, Banky interrupts to ask what a 'Nubian' is, momentarily disrupting the intensity of the speech.

entities.name: Hooper describes Death Star destruction as intergalactic gentrification
entities.description: Hooper reframes the Rebel Alliance's destruction of the Death Star as a form of racialized gentrification, where white forces displace black power structures in the name of safety for white citizens.

entities.name: Holden counters that Vader and Luke reconcile as family
entities.description: Holden attempts to challenge Hooper's interpretation by pointing out that Vader is Luke's father and that they ultimately form a bond in Return of the Jedi, suggesting a redemptive arc.

entities.name: Hooper condemns Vader's unmasking as symbolic betrayal
entities.description: Hooper expresses outrage at the revelation of Anakin Skywalker's white face beneath Vader's mask, interpreting it as a message that black identity is superficial and that inner aspiration toward whiteness is inevitable.

entities.name: Banky admits he believes everyone wants to be white
entities.description: In response to Hooper's critique, Banky bluntly states that the idea of internalized desire to be white might actually be true, provoking further tension.

entities.name: lightsaber
entities.description: A weapon in the Star Wars universe that becomes a symbol of power and control in Hooper's racial allegory of the films.

entities.name: Hooper draws gun and shoots Banky with blanks
entities.description: Hooper pulls a nine millimeter firearm from his belt, aims at Banky, and fires, causing Banky to fall forward into the crowd; the gun is later revealed to contain blank rounds.

entities.name: Crowd reacts to gunfire and scatters
entities.description: After Hooper fires the gun, the crowd screams in panic and quickly disperses from the scene.

entities.name: Hooper performs 'Black Rage' act on stage
entities.description: Hooper jumps over a table, raises his fists, and shouts 'BLACK RAGE!' repeatedly in a theatrical performance meant to project a violent, racially charged persona.

entities.name: Hooper breaks character and reveals performance
entities.description: After the staged shooting, Hooper steps off the stage, lifts Banky's head, and breaks character by laughing and speaking in his natural voice, revealing the entire event as a scripted act.

entities.name: Banky expresses surprise at performance intensity
entities.description: Banky comments that he didn't expect Hooper to shout 'Black Rage' and admits he nearly lost control of his bladder from shock.

entities.name: Holden questions legitimacy of Hooper's public performances
entities.description: Holden expresses disbelief that Hooper can stage such violent acts in public without police intervention, questioning how he avoids legal consequences.

entities.name: Hooper explains use of blanks and publisher approval
entities.description: Hooper reveals the gun was loaded with blanks and that his publisher, Opiate, obtains legal clearances and actively encourages the theatrical performances to promote his image and book sales.

entities.name: Hooper and Banky share a kiss during backstage interaction
entities.description: Hooper kisses Banky full on the lips in a playful or intimate gesture, which Banky responds to by wiping his lips and rejecting further physical involvement.

entities.name: Banky refuses romantic or sexual role in performance
entities.description: After being kissed, Banky clarifies that while he will play the role of Hooper's victim in the act, he will not participate in a romantic or sexual dynamic with him.

entities.description: A participant in Hooper's performance, playing the role of victim on stage and engaging in a personal, ambiguous relationship with Hooper backstage.

entities.name: Alyssa confronts Hooper about dominating panel discussions
entities.description: Alyssa approaches Hooper and expresses frustration that his performance consistently ends the panel, overshadowing her opportunity to speak, despite knowing the publisher arranges it.

entities.name: Hooper introduces Alyssa to Holden and Banky
entities.description: Hooper presents Alyssa Jones to Holden and Banky, identifying her as the author of 'Idiosyncratic Routine' and noting their shared history on multiple panels.

entities.name: Banky makes dismissive comment about Alyssa's book
entities.description: Banky tells Alyssa he has read her book and describes it as 'cute' and 'chick stuff,' prompting Holden to physically reprimand him.

entities.name: Holden apologizes to Alyssa for Banky's behavior
entities.description: Holden shoots Banky a disapproving look and apologizes to Alyssa, explaining Banky's rudeness as a result of his struggles with being an inker.

entities.name: Alyssa responds sarcastically to Holden's compliment
entities.description: Alyssa acknowledges Holden's praise of her book but replies with sarcasm, suggesting he would only be welcome on future panels if he changed his race or lost his penis.

entities.name: Hooper invites Alyssa for a post-rave drink

entities.name: Holden agrees to stay for drinks despite Banky's hesitation
entities.description: When Banky indicates they should leave, Holden overrides him and agrees to stay, prompting a puzzled look from Banky before he reluctantly consents.

entities.name: Hooper claims Archie and Jughead were lovers
entities.description: Hooper states that Archie and Jughead had a romantic relationship, with Archie as the submissive partner and Jughead as the dominant one, citing Jughead's hat as symbolic of his role.

entities.name: Banky rejects Hooper's interpretation of Archie comics
entities.description: Banky angrily dismisses Hooper's claim about Archie and Jughead's relationship, expressing outrage and discomfort with the suggestion.

entities.name: Holden acknowledges ambiguity in Archie's romantic choices
entities.description: Holden comments that Hooper has a valid point, noting that Archie never definitively chose between Betty and Veronica, suggesting possible bisexuality or indecision.

entities.name: Banky accuses Archie of wanting a threesome with Betty and Veronica
entities.description: Banky argues that Archie's inability to choose between Betty and Veronica stems from his desire to have both in a sexual relationship, not from any homosexual tendencies.

entities.name: Hooper challenges Banky to buy a clue with a dollar
entities.description: Hooper hands Banky a dollar and sarcastically instructs him to go to the corner store to 'buy himself a clue' about the true nature of Archie's character.

entities.name: Banky insults Hooper and refuses the dollar
entities.description: Banky tells Hooper to 'eat it' and calls him 'Urkel' in a derogatory manner, rejecting the offered dollar and escalating the tension.

entities.name: Hooper warns Banky about using the name Urkel
entities.description: Hooper confronts Banky for calling him Urkel, indicating that the nickname is offensive or provocative in their context.

entities.name: Banky confronts Hooper and demands he return to the comic store
entities.description: Banky stands up and insists that Hooper accompany him back across the street to purchase more Archie comics to prove his argument about Archie's heterosexuality.

entities.name: Hooper agrees to accompany Banky as a mock therapist
entities.description: Hooper playfully frames himself as a 'mother-therapist' who will help Banky work through his emotional conflict about the Archie comics, then gets up to leave with him.

entities.name: Banky and Hooper leave the table to go to the comic store
entities.description: Banky and Hooper exit the booth and leave the location, heading back across the street to retrieve Archie comics for their debate.

entities.name: Alyssa and Holden are left alone at the table
entities.description: After Banky and Hooper depart, Alyssa and Holden remain behind, now isolated from the group discussion and setting up a private moment between them.

entities.name: Hooper confronts Holden about Banky's absence
entities.description: Hooper asks Holden about the whereabouts of his partner Banky, initiating a conversation about Banky's emotional state and his discomfort with Holden's relationship with Alyssa.

entities.name: Holden reveals Banky is sulking over Alyssa situation
entities.description: Holden explains to Hooper that Banky is upset and struggling emotionally with Holden's relationship with Alyssa, indicating tension within their friendship.

entities.name: Hooper accuses Banky of homophobia
entities.description: Hooper suggests that Banky is grappling with repressed feelings and homophobic attitudes, interpreting Banky's reaction to Holden's relationship as rooted in discomfort with non-heteronormative dynamics.

entities.name: Holden denies Banky hates gays but acknowledges his discomfort
entities.description: Holden defends Banky by stating he doesn't hate gay people, but concedes that Banky may have homophobic tendencies, especially in light of recent events involving Alyssa.

entities.name: Hooper suggests Banky has lost Holden to the dark side
entities.description: Hooper frames Banky's perception of losing Holden as a personal and emotional betrayal, symbolically casting Alyssa as the corrupting influence representing 'the dark side'.

entities.name: Holden clarifies he and Banky were not in a romantic relationship
entities.description: Holden reacts with surprise and corrects Hooper's implication that his bond with Banky was romantic, emphasizing the platonic nature of their friendship.

entities.name: Hooper implies Banky has deep unacknowledged feelings for Holden
entities.description: Hooper suggests that Banky's intense reaction stems from repressed romantic or emotional love for Holden that he is not ready to confront.

entities.name: Holden reveals Banky has been investigating Alyssa
entities.description: Holden discloses that Banky has been actively gathering negative information about Alyssa, indicating obsessive or intrusive behavior.

entities.name: Holden shares rumor about Alyssa having sex with two men
entities.description: Holden tells Hooper that Banky heard a rumor claiming Alyssa engaged in sexual activity with two men simultaneously, which has affected Holden emotionally.

entities.name: Hooper mocks the rumor and questions its relevance
entities.description: Hooper responds to the rumor with sarcasm, suggesting it undermines Banky's attempt to discredit Alyssa as non-heterosexual and therefore fails to serve his agenda.

entities.name: Holden expresses emotional disturbance over the rumor
entities.description: Despite claiming he shouldn't care, Holden admits that the idea of Alyssa being with multiple men at once has unsettled him, revealing internalized biases.

entities.name: Hooper challenges Holden on double standards regarding sexuality
entities.description: Hooper confronts Holden for being disturbed by Alyssa's potential sexual history with men while being unbothered by the idea of her with women, accusing him of subscribing to 'lesbian chic'.

entities.name: Hooper critiques societal preference for lesbian relationships over gay male relationships
entities.description: Hooper expresses frustration that society romanticizes lesbian relationships as cute or fashionable while marginalizing gay men, especially gay Black men like himself.

entities.name: Hooper reveals personal alienation as a gay Black man
entities.description: Hooper articulates his sense of isolation, feeling unsupported even within the LGBTQ+ community and facing compounded discrimination due to race, sexuality, and gender expression.

entities.description: Holden and Hooper spend time looking through a collection of laser discs, using the activity as a backdrop for their conversation about relationships and identity.
